question.content:
Anju tried to define a reflection.

- For any point $R$ on the line of reflection $\ell$ , the image $R'$ is at the same point as $R$.
- For any point $P$ **not** on the line of reflection $\ell$, the image $P'$ is on the other side of $\ell$ such that $\overline{PP'}$ is perpendicular to $\ell$.

**What mistake did Anju make in her definition of a reflection?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.clue: Reflections map points on one side of the line of reflection to the other side. If $\overline{PP'}$ was parallel to $\ell$, then $P$ and $P'$ would be on the same side of $\ell$.
choices.content: $\overline{PP'}$ must be parallel to the line of reflection, not perpendicular.

choices.clue: If we don't mention these distances, we could construct a new line that passes through $P$ and is perpendicular to $\ell$. Then $P'$ could be any point on this new line that is on the other side of $\ell$.
choices.content: Points $P$ and $P'$ must be the same distance from the line of reflection.

choices.clue: Reflections map points on one side of the line of reflection to the other side, so we don't need to specify a direction when we define a reflection.
choices.content: Anju needed to include the direction of the reflection.

choices.clue: There is more than one possible point $P'$ we could draw from Anju's definition. What additional information does the definition need to clarify which point is the image of point $P$?
choices.content: Anju did not make a mistake.
